leadIn: By the end of this lesson, learners will be able to:
objectives: Apply the useState hook to initialize and manage state variables within a custom hook.
Use the useRef hook to create a mutable reference that persists across component renders.
Implement a custom hook function with TypeScript generics to handle different data types.
Execute conditional logic to check if a value has changed between renders.
Utilize the useEffect hook to perform side effects after component renders.
Assign previous values to a ref's current property for persistence across renders.
Access the current property of a ref to retrieve stored previous values.
Construct a custom hook that returns the previous value of a given state or prop.
Control the timing of effect execution by specifying dependencies in useEffect.
Define TypeScript interfaces or types for custom hook return values when needed.
Invoke the custom usePrevious hook within functional components to track value changes.
Return the stored previous value from the custom hook for use in component logic.
